persistent_identifier_status: Repository-local identifier for this transcription; the DOI identifies the source article, not this derived dataset.
title: Italian ryegrass silage fermentative losses and aerobic exposure outcomes
citation: Assis, J. A., Carbonare, M. S. D., & Schmidt, P. (2026). Different dry matter contents on the fermentation and preservation of wilted ryegrass silage with or without microbial inoculants. Revista Brasileira de Zootecnia, 55. https://doi.org/10.37496/rbz5520250112
source_locations: Methods sections 2.1–2.3 for loss and aerobic stability protocols
Results sections 3.1–3.2 for missing pH samples
geography: Forage grown at a commercial farm in Castro, Paraná, Brazil; aerobic exposure was conducted in a temperature-controlled room at the research facility in Paraná, Brazil.
license: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0), stated on the article page. Cite the article and retain the license attribution.
material_scope: Wilted Italian ryegrass silage (Lolium multiflorum L., cultivar F ABC 1) after 62 days of ensiling, assessed by DM target and inoculant treatment; silo opening followed by a separate aerobic exposure test.
experimental_conditions: Five replicate silos per treatment combination. Aerobic stability was defined as elapsed time until silage temperature reached 26 °C, approximately 2 °C above the room average of 24.5 ± 1.4 °C. Approximately 2 kg was loosely held in a 20-L bucket for 20 days; temperature was recorded every 30 minutes. DM loss during aerobic exposure was assessed after 10 days. pH was scheduled for days 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, and 20; Table 3 additionally reports day 18, while the paper states no pH samples were collected between days 10 and 18 because of a technical failure.
data_scope: Fourteen Table 3 properties are transcribed in the table's treatment-group layout, including fermentative DM/gas/effluent losses, aerobic stability and temperature endpoints, 10-day aerobic DM loss, and pH observations. Values, significance letters, DM-group means, and P-values are retained.
table_layout: One row per reported property; treatment values are kept in separate columns corresponding to Table 3. Cell strings preserve significance letters and negative source-reported losses. This is a table-native transcription, not a normalized runtime parameter table.
limitations: Reference-only; no GreenHub runtime parameter or default is mapped to these observations.
The feed is cultivated Italian ryegrass in Brazil, not Dutch roadside grass or project-specific VARTA feedstock.
Negative DM and gas loss values for the 32% DM INO treatment are retained literally; the study does not justify interpreting them as a physical production pathway or correcting them.
Aerobic stability is tied to this study's loose-bucket geometry, room temperature, 26 °C threshold, and 20-day protocol; it is not a silo storage degradation rate.
DMLae is measured after 10 days of aerobic exposure; it must not be treated as a 20-day loss.
The source reports a technical failure in pH sampling between days 10 and 18; no values are available for days 12, 14, or 16 and no interpolation is performed.
Treatment means and significance tests do not provide raw replicate data or standard deviations in the table.
conversion_or_processing: Table 3 means, units, significance letters, and P-values were transcribed without numeric conversion, imputation, clamping, interpolation, kinetic fitting, or activation. The source's 60 °C DM basis is retained for losses.
uncertainty: Five silo replicates were used per treatment combination. Standard deviations and raw replicate values are not supplied in Table 3; inferential results and significance letters are reproduced as reported.
